observed_evidence: At the UN General Assembly on September 22, President Donald Trump publicly threatened Iran with annihilation if no deal is reached and called for Tehran to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz and return to negotiations.

After the speech, Trump said U.S. and Iranian officials had met on the UN sidelines; high-quality reporting described this as the first confirmed direct contact between the two sides since the war began in February.
The direct contact creates a diplomatic channel, but no ceasefire, Hormuz reopening agreement, sanctions relief, or verified energy-shipping normalization was announced.
semantic_interpretation: The new direct contact modestly improves diplomatic optionality, but the simultaneous explicit U.S. escalation threat keeps tail risk high. This is a two-sided event rather than a verified de-escalation. Semantic scoring must not overwrite official oil, inflation, rates, FX, shipping or macro series.
